images.seen: A woman with a glass of white wine on the stone stoep steps of a Karoo farmhouse at a blazing orange sunset, windpomp silhouetted on the plain. Sunday.
lines: The day finally dropped below thirty and the stoep is collecting the reward.
A sky like that is what forty degrees looks like on its way out.
First sittable hour since breakfast, and it brought colours.

images.seen: Three friends walking the palm-lined beachfront promenade at sunset, soft-serve cones already melting over their hands. Friday.
lines: The soft-serve is losing a race it was never going to win.
The promenade fills up the minute the temperature becomes friendly again.
Still warm enough at sunset that the ice cream is doing the sweating.

images.seen: A sweating glass of ice water standing on the promenade wall at night, bicycles leaning on the rail, a family strolling under the streetlights. Sunday.
lines: The glass is sweating at nine at night, which tells you about today.
The whole promenade came out after dark, when the town becomes walkable again.
Night has not cooled anything yet; even the water is perspiring.

images.seen: A family asleep on mattresses laid out on the stoep under a huge Milky Way, one boy still awake watching a bat cross the stars. Friday.
lines: Too hot for walls tonight: the whole family moved the bedroom outside.
The house held the day's heat, so the beds came out to the stars.
One member of the sleep-out is doing exactly none of the sleeping.
